title: Device status lookup with cached fallback
name: Device status service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code degrades when the telemetry gateway is unhealthy? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What does a caller of getStatus receive when the gateway is down, the breaker has been open for a while, and the cache holds a reading observed 3 minutes ago (assuming a max staleness of 10 minutes)?
choices: A StatusUnavailableException, since an open breaker never serves cached data
The cached reading with degraded set to true
The cached reading unchanged, indistinguishable from a fresh one
A CallNotPermittedException propagated to the caller

questions.prompt: What happens in lastKnownStatus when the cached reading for the device is 40 minutes old and max staleness is 10 minutes?
choices: The stale reading is returned with degraded set to true
The cache evicts the entry and the gateway is called again
getUsable returns empty and a StatusUnavailableException is thrown with the original cause attached
An empty Optional is returned to the caller of getStatus

questions.prompt: Why does StatusCache.put use ConcurrentHashMap.merge with an observedAt comparison instead of a plain put?
choices: merge is required for ConcurrentHashMap to be thread safe
It prevents an older reading, finished later by a slow request, from overwriting a newer one
It avoids storing duplicate readings with identical timestamps in memory
It makes the entry expire automatically after maxStaleness
